name: EMA Crossback

card.context: A liquid leader (RS 80 or more) above its 200-day that has just started a new up-cycle: a Wedge Pop (a close back above the 9 and 20 EMA out of a tight range on volume) or a breakout, 3 to 20 sessions earlier, the 9 EMA above a rising 20 EMA. Green or Yellow market, early in its cycle.
card.pattern: The first pullback since the pop: a 2 to 10 session sideways or slow drift from the post-pop high into the 9/20 zone, and a hold day whose low reaches the zone (down to 1% under the 20 EMA) and closes at or above the 20 EMA in the upper half of its range.
card.trigger: PREV DAY HIGH BREAK: buy at market as price trades a few cents above the hold day's high on any of the next 3 sessions; after that the setup is stale. A 30 or 65-minute breakout or red to green on the hold day is the advanced version.
card.stop: A few cents under the hold day's low, usually 1 to 3% away; size down past 3%, skip past 5% or past the stock's average daily range.
card.failure_mode: The hold day's low breaks before or just after the trigger, or the stock closes under the 20 EMA on heavy volume and the 9 crosses under the 20. Late crossbacks (long after the pop, or after an Exhaustion Extension) and crossbacks taken with the Nasdaq under its 20 EMA fail most.

criteria.statement: The course teaches Kell's definition: the first pullback into the rising 10 and 20-day EMAs (our 9/20) after a stock has turned up out of a decline (his Wedge Pop) or broken out. Not the house text's re-entry after an extension.

measure.what: the stage of Kell's cycle the crossback follows
measure.value: the Wedge Pop (or a breakout), before any Base n' Break or Exhaustion Extension

options.basis: Kell's: the first pullback into the rising averages right after a Wedge Pop or breakout; the dossier's recommendation; D-002's default (the card, playbook, lesson and definitions.json are corrected)
the house text: a re-entry after an extension, with the averages crossing (the Model Book card and playbook, the UCT Method lesson, SET.15)

a_plus: xbk.wedge_pop_first: the first crossback after a powerful Wedge Pop, a gap, heavy volume, a close at the top of the range (Most Wedge Pops that lead to new, powerful trends start with gaps)

xbk.leadership: a true leader, it turned before the market, RS near the top, strong earnings and sales growth (xbk.fundamentals)
xbk.index_20ema: the market is itself starting a new up-cycle (an index Wedge Pop or follow-through)
xbk.weekly: the weekly chart in an uptrend and not stretched far above its 10-week line

xbk.stop_width: a deep or violent pullback, heavy-volume down days, a close under the 20 EMA, a stop over 3%
xbk.averages: the 9 EMA flattening toward the 20; the 50-day flat

lookalikes.tell: Count the sessions since the stock closed back above both the 9 and 20 EMA out of a decline, and count the tests since. The first test of the averages 3 to 20 sessions after that Wedge Pop is the Crossback; a tap of a 20 EMA that has been rising for weeks, after a 1.5 ATR advance off the line, is the 20 EMA Pullback.

Ask whether the averages were just reclaimed or just held. A Wedge Pop is the day that closes back above both EMAs out of a tight range after at least 8 of 15 closes under the 20 EMA; the Crossback is the pullback after it that holds the averages with the 9 still above the 20. One close back over the 20 EMA is a pop setting up, not a crossback.

Count the rests since the pop and look at where the buy is. Kell's Base n' Break is the second or later rest, a 5 to 15 session base near the highs bought through its pivot into new highs; the Crossback is the first rest, bought a few cents over the hold day's high at the averages.

Ask which line and whether it was lost. A Crossback holds the rising 9 and 20 EMA with no run of closes under them; a Remount is a 50-day or 200-day line lost for 5 or more consecutive closes and then retaken.

Measure the pole and the place. A bull flag needs a 20% or larger gain inside 20 sessions and a 3 to 15 session tight drift that gives back at most half of it, anywhere above the 20 EMA; the Crossback's drift must reach the 9/20 zone, needs no pole, and follows a Wedge Pop or breakout 3 to 20 sessions earlier.

invalidations: Before the trigger: the hold day's low breaks (xbk.inv_low_break).
Before the trigger: no trigger within 3 sessions (xbk.inv_stale).
Before the trigger: a close under the 20-day EMA on above-average volume (xbk.inv_heavy_close_under).
The 9-day EMA crosses under the 20-day EMA (xbk.inv_cross).
Not the first test, or after an Exhaustion Extension (xbk.inv_late_cycle).
The stock's own history of failed crossbacks, or crossbacks failing all around on low volume (xbk.inv_failed_history).
Earnings within 3 sessions; price under the 200-day; RS under 80 (xbk.earnings_window, xbk.above_200, xbk.leadership).
After entry: the stop; under 1R after 10 sessions, out (xbk.stop, xbk.time_stop).
mistakes: Buying the touch before buyers show (no hold day, no trigger).
Calling a late-trend pullback, or a pullback after an Exhaustion Extension, a crossback (our own house text makes this mistake).
Buying while the 9 is under the 20.

Mixing it up with the Wedge Pop: one close back over the 20 EMA is a pop setting up, not a crossback (Bracco; Kell: Many traders mistakenly believe the Wedge Pop is simply about crossing the moving averages).
Re-buying the same consolidating stock again and again (Kell's 2-3x lesson; E56).
Buying under the 200-day or into earnings (B26, B22).

short_mirror.note: The Downside EMA Crossback, which Kell defines exactly (S4) and D47 mirrors (dossier 8.6): a close below the 200-day SMA (B26), preferably a falling one; RS 20 or less, weakest groups (C31 mirror); borrow available and cheap (D48); a Red market (D46, F65); a Wedge Drop 3 to 20 sessions earlier (a close back under both EMAs after a run above them); the 9-day EMA under the 20-day, both falling; the first rally into the 9/20 zone stalls with a close at or under the 20-day EMA in the lower half of its range; short with a market order a few cents under that rejection day's low; stop a few cents over its high. Kell: Enter the short position when weakness drags the price through the pivot; only In more severe market conditions, and Stay in cash is his default. The dossier recommends teaching it as a Red-market short only (question 9); D-001's shared default is recognition only until he shows examples. Not scanned. The Model Book card's short side (one of the four climax-day entries for the Parabolic Short) is not Kell's downside crossback, which follows a Wedge Drop, not a climax (5.4).

best_conditions: The start of a new market up-cycle: the index has just made its own Wedge Pop or follow-through, and leaders are crossing back while the index is still pulling back (UCT 2026-04-12: Now looking for continuation and crossback).
